hints: Does tilting an angle on the page change how far apart its arms have turned?
Every figure here measures 90 degrees between its arms, regardless of tilt, so count all 3 of them.

canonical: A right angle is defined by its measure (90 degrees between its arms), not by whether it looks upright on the page.
Every one of the 3 figures measures exactly 90 degrees, so all 3 of them are right angles.

stem: 3 angles are drawn around a page, each tilted at a different angle from upright, but every single one has its arms turned exactly a quarter of a full turn apart (90 degrees). A student who believes a right angle must sit upright, like a wall meeting a floor, refuses to count any of them as right angles, insisting there are 0 right angles among the 3 figures. Using the correct definition (a right angle is any angle measuring exactly 90 degrees, tilted or not), how many of the 3 figures are actually right angles?
